changes.headline: Thursday settled lower, Asia bought back the new Hormuz tanker tactic, and the reserve release programme is fully awarded
changes.dek: Thursday settles: Brent Dec26 $114.88 (was $115.32 Wednesday), WTI Dec26 $102.00 (was $102.78); spread $12.88 (was $12.54). Asia at 0323 GMT Fri: Brent Dec $116.08, Brent Jan $112.19, WTI $103.37 (Reuters). DOE Oct 29: awards of more than 40 Mbbl complete the 172 Mbbl release commitment; return of more than 216 Mbbl including 44 premium from early next year. Diesel crack $90.42, a sixth close below $100.. Brent settled at $114.88, down $0.44, and WTI at $102.00, down $0.78 (settles, Oct 29), after both fell more than $2 intraday on diplomacy headlines, the European strategic release announcement and added Chinese fuel export quotas. Overnight the market paid the escalation side: a small boat attached two explosive devices to an outbound tanker's hull in the Strait of Hormuz at 2212 UTC Thursday (UKMTO Warning 187-26; engine room fire, crew safe, vessel underway again), a second tanker took an unknown projectile at about 1600 UTC, and the Houthis claimed a six target wave against Saudi Arabia including a second strike claim on Ras Tanura, unconfirmed on day three with no loading evidence. Asia traded Brent at $116.08 and WTI at $103.37 at 0323 GMT (Reuters, Oct 30). Brent December expires today; January is about $4 lower, so Monday's headline drop is the roll, not a move. The Energy Department announced Oct 29 that awards of more than 40 million barrels, including volumes from previous solicitations, complete its 172 million barrel release commitment, with more than 216 million barrels to return from early next year including 44 million premium barrels; no companies were named and no heating oil reserve award has been posted.
changes.balance_read: The physical response is now fully committed on both sides of the Atlantic: the US release programme is spent as an offset, and Europe's 42.6 million barrels (half diesel) are announced into a product market whose tightest stock lines remain 10 percent under their five year averages. What keeps the premium is not flow loss, which the gauges still put at partial recovery, but a threat that keeps changing form: mines claimed, then hull attached explosives, then a legal threat against the largest carrier from Nov 1.

changes.headline: December WCS: the traded level is Wednesday's -$31.10; Thursday's -$30.50 is one lot, and thermal supply printed records
changes.dek: ICE Oct 28 file (landed after the Oct 29 edition): TMW Dec26 -$31.10 on 200 lots, Jan27 -$29.15 on 915 lots. ICE Oct 29: TMW Dec26 -$30.50 on 1 lot, Jan27 -$28.75 on 65 lots; ARV Dec26 -$22.973 on 850 lots; ARV to TMW +$7.53 in December, +$7.95 in January. Oil Sands Magazine: third quarter thermal production averaged a record 1.8 Mb/d; September records at Foster Creek, Christina Lake North and Surmont.. Wednesday's settlement file answers the question the Oct 29 edition left open: the Canadian front did not follow flat price up; December WCS widened slightly to -$31.10 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 28) and traded 200 lots doing it, with January at -$29.15 on 915 lots. Thursday's settle tightened to -$30.50 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 29) on a single lot, while January tightened on trade to -$28.75 (65 lots) and Houston traded the week's size at -$22.973 on 850 lots. December WCS outright is $71.50 on Thursday's WTI settle. The December export spread compressed to +$7.53 while January's widened to +$7.95. The supply side behind the front printed records: Oil Sands Magazine's September review (Oct 29) has Alberta thermal production at a record third quarter average of 1.8 Mb/d, September all time highs at Foster Creek (250 kb/d) and Christina Lake North (117 kb/d), and Surmont over 157 kb/d matching its record. Two Midwest buyers are returning against that supply: Joliet continues to recover from its mid September power outage and Toledo is returning to normal rates after its turnaround (Oil Sands Magazine, Oct 29). Imperial Oil reports today (call 9:00 a.m. MT); its release was not out at the 02:05 MDT check.
changes.balance_read: The front month's honest level is the one that traded: December at about minus thirty one, January at about minus twenty nine and tightening on volume. Record thermal supply argues the wide persists; returning Midwest runs and a Houston leg trading 850 lots argue the barrels that can move are finding bids. The one lot December tightening is a mark, not a turn.

changes.headline: The product supply response arrived on paper: Europe releases, Russia exports, and freight finds its floor argument
changes.dek: Europe: 42.6 Mbbl by end January, 20.5 of it diesel (Oct 29). Russia: diesel export ban extended to year end, November quotas quadruple to 2 Mt, about 0.5 Mb/d; refinery runs rebounded 350 kb/d to 4.0 Mb/d. Freight: 63 attack disabled tankers still out of service including 20 VLCCs (McQuilling via RBN, Oct 29); Atlantic VLCC rates down 27 to 32 percent from peaks (Vortexa, Oct 28).. Three supply responses landed in one window. Twelve European countries will release 42.6 million barrels from strategic reserves by end January, including 20.5 million barrels of diesel, completing the coordinated 400 million barrel action; France's 10 million barrel diesel tranche reaches the market in the coming days, sold at cost. Russia extended its diesel export ban to year end while quadrupling November quota exports to 2 million tonnes to fulfil its US arrangement, and its refinery runs rebounded 350 kb/d last week to 4.0 Mb/d after no confirmed attacks since Oct 15 (Reuters, Oct 29). A reported Ukrainian strike on the Novokuybyshevsk refinery overnight Oct 29 to 30 is unconfirmed as to damage (ASTRA, Oct 30). On freight, the correction now has a stated floor: 63 tankers disabled by attacks in 2026 remain out of service, repairs run one to three months, and only 22 sanctioned VLCCs under 20 years old could realistically return to conventional trading (McQuilling via RBN, Oct 29); Vortexa (Oct 28) counts Atlantic VLCC rates down 27 percent (US Gulf) and 32 percent (West Africa) from peaks with ballasters rising, the same floor conclusion. West African trade firmed one day against the trend on Thursday, a 40 point VLCC Worldscale rise (Reuters, Oct 29).
changes.balance_read: The diesel crisis trade is being answered with announced barrels on three continents at once, which is why the crack has closed below $100 six straight times. The freight leg of the Canadian differential is different: the rate correction is real, but the fleet arithmetic (disabled hulls, drydock, a thin returnable sanctioned fleet) argues the level stays far above pre war, so the delivered cost pressure on distant heavy barrels fades slowly, not suddenly.

flags.title: Hormuz tactics and Saudi claims: a hull attached explosive attack is verified; Ras Tanura is day three unconfirmed; the carrier action date is Nov 1
flags.detail: UKMTO Warning 187-26 (Oct 29, 2212 UTC): a small boat attached two explosive devices to an outbound tanker's hull northeast of Khasab; engine room fire, crew safe, vessel underway again. A second tanker took an unknown projectile the same day (Warning 186-26). October's incident count is a record 29 (IMO via Vortexa). Iran's guard claimed three mine strikes and its army a fourth; the US Central Command position (Oct 28) is that the mine claims are false and primary routes remain cleared. Vortexa's preliminary October loadings west of Hormuz run about 11 Mb/d against 14.5 pre war, about 6 Mb/d of it by ship to ship transfer. The Houthis claimed six Saudi targets on Oct 29 including a second Ras Tanura strike; the coalition confirmed interceptions only, and no statement addresses damage at Ras Tanura, Abqaiq or Rabigh, with no loading interruption reported. From Nov 1 the strait authority threatens legal action against all vessels of the carrier behind 47 percent of September's Hormuz VLCC transits. Trade the loadings, not the claim count. Trigger: A Saudi or Aramco damage statement, loading evidence of an interruption at any named facility, enforcement against a vessel of the threatened carrier on or after Nov 1, or a tier 1 flow print stepping down

flags.title: Reserve programme status: the US release is fully awarded and Europe's is announced; the heating oil reserve award is still missing
flags.detail: The Energy Department's Oct 29 awards of more than 40 million barrels complete the 172 million barrel US release commitment, with more than 216 million barrels to return from early next year including 44 million premium barrels. No awardee companies were named, and the posted contracts page exposed no table to re-sum, so no verified new borrower tally exists; the last verified tally (133.56 million barrels, 13 companies, Oct 13) is superseded as a status. Europe's 42.6 million barrel release, half diesel, completes the coordinated 400 million barrel action on the announcement side. The Northeast heating oil reserve exchange (bids closed Oct 27, deliveries by Nov 13) still has no award posted. The reserve stock stands at 282.6 million barrels, the lowest since October 1982: the release offset is committed, and what remains is delivery scheduling. Trigger: A posted awardee list or contracts table from the Department, a heating oil reserve award posting, or the first delivered French diesel cargoes from the European release

flags.title: Sanctions waiver: three cargoes, a fertilizer dispute, and a disclosure deadline tomorrow
flags.detail: The first waiver tanker still declares no destination (for orders). A tracking service assesses the two later St. Petersburg departures are carrying UAN fertilizer, not diesel; fertilizer is not sanctioned and is authorised for import, which would remove those hulls from the legal dispute. Other reporting describes the cargoes as diesel; the question is unresolved on the public record. An environmental group's tracking names seven US bound tankers totalling 288,000 tonnes; no US delivery of any waiver cargo has been confirmed. The senator's letter demanding the first ship's owner recall it and disclose the seller, buyer, charterer, insurer and terminal operator reaches its deadline on Saturday Oct 31, and New Jersey's governor is examining options to keep the tankers out of her state's ports. Russia's diesel export ban extends to year end with November quotas at 2 million tonnes. Trigger: A response to the Oct 31 letter, a confirmed US delivery or port refusal, or cargo documentation resolving the diesel versus fertilizer question

flags.title: November apportionment 19 percent lights and 7 percent heavies; the December call is unregistered; December WCS's traded level is -$31.10
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment is Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, Oct 20), with Light 13 percent at Cromer and Heavy 16 percent at Superior. December's outlook is persistence at the same levels; no judgment call is registered, and nominations close Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST. Trans Mountain's October apportionment was 7 percent. The December WCS level that traded volume this week is -$31.10 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 28, 200 lots); Thursday's -$30.50 settle rested on 1 lot, while January traded both days and tightened to -$28.75. Thermal supply printed third quarter records into the constraint. Trigger: A registered December judgment call, a December WCS print on real volume through -$31.00 or a traded tightening, or the December apportionment notice after nominations close
